check_email.description: Find out whether an email address appears in any known data breach, and in which ones by name. An address in no breach comes back with 'breached' set to false rather than failing the step. XposedOrNot allows 25 email checks an hour from Lodol. No API key required.

mock_response.summary: test@example.com appears in 3 known data breaches.

check_email.name: check_email

parameters.description: The email address to look up, such as name@example.com. Spaces and capitals don't matter.
parameters.name: email

breach_count.description: How many known breaches the address appears in.

breached.description: True when the address appears in at least one known breach.

breaches.description: The names of those breaches, A to Z. Empty when there are none.

email.description: The address checked, trimmed and in lower case.

summary.description: One sentence with the answer, ready for a message.

check_password.description: Find out whether a password has been leaked in a data breach, and how often it was seen. The password never leaves Lodol: it is hashed here and only the first 10 characters of its hash are sent, which match many passwords. Useful for refusing leaked passwords at sign-up. No API key required.
check_password.display_str_template: Check whether a password has been leaked.

mock_response.summary: This password has been exposed in data breaches, seen 62,703 times. Don't use it.

check_password.name: check_password

parameters.description: The password to check. Only the first 10 characters of its Keccak-512 hash are sent to XposedOrNot, never the password itself. Pass it from an earlier step rather than typing a real password here, since a typed value is saved with the workflow.
parameters.name: password

exposed.description: True when the password appears in leaked password lists.

hash_prefix.description: The only thing sent to XposedOrNot: the first 10 characters of the password's Keccak-512 hash.

summary.description: One sentence with the answer, ready for a message.

times_seen.description: How many times it was seen in breaches. 0 when not found.

get_breach.description: Get one data breach by its name: what happened, when, the website, how many records and what kinds of data were exposed, how passwords were stored, and a news report about it. Takes the names 'Check an email for breaches' returns. A name XposedOrNot does not have fails the step. No API key required.

mock_response.description: Adobe, the multinational software company, suffered a major data breach in October 2013 that eventually affected about 150 million accounts.
mock_response.name: Adobe

get_breach.name: get_breach

parameters.description: The breach's name in XposedOrNot, such as Adobe or LinkedIn. Pick one, or pass a name from an earlier step. Capitals don't matter.
parameters.name: breach

added_at.description: When XposedOrNot added the breach, as an ISO 8601 date and time.

breach_type.description: What kind of leak it was: 'Data breach', 'Combo list' (credentials gathered from many leaks), 'Stealer logs' or 'Scrape'.

breached_on.description: When the breach happened, as a date (YYYY-MM-DD). XposedOrNot records the month, so this is the first day of it.

description.description: What happened and what was exposed, in a few sentences.

domain.description: The website that was breached, such as 'adobe.com'.

exposed_data.description: The kinds of data exposed, such as 'Email addresses' and 'Passwords'.

industry.description: The breached organisation's industry, such as 'Finance'.

name.description: The breach's name in XposedOrNot, such as 'Adobe'. Get a breach takes it.

password_risk.description: How the breached passwords were stored: 'plaintext', 'easytocrack', 'hardtocrack' or 'unknown'.

password_risk_label.description: The same in words, such as 'Easy to crack'.

records_exposed.description: How many accounts or records were exposed.

reference_url.description: A news report or announcement about the breach, when there is one.

sensitive.description: True for a breach whose membership is itself sensitive, such as a dating site. Email checks don't name these.

verified.description: True when XposedOrNot has confirmed the breach is genuine.

get_domain_summary.description: Find out how exposed a company's email domain is: how many addresses at it appear in known breaches, in how many breaches, how many pastes, and when the latest breach happened. Counts only; no addresses are returned. A domain with nothing exposed comes back with 'exposed' set to false. No API key required.

An address in no breach comes back with 'breached' set to false. No API key required.

description: Check whether an email address or a password has been exposed in a known data breach, with XposedOrNot's free, open breach index. Get an address's full breach history with a risk score, see how exposed a company's email domain is, look up and list breaches, follow breach news, and run a workflow whenever a new breach is added. Passwords are checked without ever leaving Lodol. No account or API key required.

xposedornot_new_breach_trigger.description: Runs when XposedOrNot adds a data breach to its index, optionally only for one website or industry. XposedOrNot is checked once an hour.
